honesty.live_l1_note: pid 31213 gravity_deepseek_v4_fullseq_capture L1 frozen export (max-layer 42) was running throughout (~90-98% of ONE core, GPU Device Utilization often 60-70% with intermittent 0% windows). Speedups are lower bounds under GPU/driver contention; remeasure when machine is idle before full-scale roll-out.

method: Sampled live L1 capture (pid 31213) via ps %cpu + ioreg IOAccelerator Device/Renderer Utilization over 5s
Short bounded probe in this worktree: synthetic limit=4, max-layer 0 then 1, max-seq-len 3, --export-host-activations, concurrent ioreg sampler
Receipt metal counters: metal_dispatches, command_buffers, cpu_visible_waits

live_l1_process.interpretation: Single-threaded host orchestration; GPU is partially utilized in bursts but host serial path (1 of 28 cores) remains the control plane. Not pure GPU-idle as sometimes observed mid-export/setup; not GPU-saturated either.

serial_bottleneck_identified.primary: Host-side serial staging between Metal dispatches: ~5 cpu_visible_waits per token×layer (command-buffer commit + wait_until_completed style sync). Process is single-core bound (~97% of one core) while 27 cores idle.
serial_bottleneck_identified.secondary: Per-token/layer host work: buffer SHA-256 for capture sites, optional host export (bf16→f32 mean-pool copy), expert bundle resolve, JSON trace assembly. npy write is end-of-run and small at this scale (4×4096 f32).
serial_bottleneck_identified.not_primary: Raw Metal kernel throughput alone (GPU Device Util often 60%+ under load but process still 1-thread CPU-bound between waits).
serial_bottleneck_identified.not_layer_shardable_without_residual_han: Layer L>0 input is previous layer child residual in-process; multi-worker layer ranges would change the graph unless residuals are exported/imported.

sharding_design.approach: Multi-process sequence sharding with distinct output directories + offline merge

cli_flags_added.--seq-end: exclusive end index; default = corpus length
cli_flags_added.--worker-id: optional label recorded in receipt.shard for merge provenance
cli_flags_added.--min-layer: must be 0; >0 hard-errors with residual-handoff explanation

sharding_design.isolation_rule: Each worker MUST use a distinct --out-dir (traces/ + activations/). Shared fixed path receipts/dsv4f_fullseq_capture_receipt.json is skipped when sharding.

merge_tool.inputs: N worker out-dirs each with DSV4F_FULLSEQ_CAPTURE_RECEIPT.json
merge_tool.safety: refuses overlapping [seq_start,seq_end) ranges; refuses duplicate example_ids

layer_sharding.reason: residual handoff across workers not implemented; --min-layer > 0 errors closed

correctness_proof.conclusion: Sequence sharding does not change the math; only wall-clock. Merged npy files are byte-identical to a single serial process on the same slice.

real_measured_speedup.workload: synthetic limit=4, max_layer=1, max_seq-len=3, export-host-activations, under concurrent live L1 capture

workers_2.note: Not 2.0x — shared Metal driver/GPU with live L1 + duplicated per-process admit/prepare startup.

workers_4.note: Multi-core host utilization proven (up to ~3.7 cores). Efficiency drops vs 2w: per-worker model admit + GPU contention + tiny 1-seq shards.

recommended_worker_count.cap_guidance: On this M3 Ultra (28 CPU / 60 GPU cores) start with N=2–4 sequence workers for full-layer captures. Re-benchmark idle-machine before N>4: 4w already showed sub-linear returns under contention. Memory: each worker reloads the gravity stream reader + Metal executors (~GB RSS each); RAM may cap N before GPU does.

why: Bit-exact correctness proven for multi-process sequence shards
Real wall-clock win: 1.4x at 2 workers and 1.8x at 4 workers even while fighting a live full L1 capture
Host was single-core bound; multi-worker converts idle CPU cores into concurrent host orchestrators feeding Metal
GPU contention caps gain below linear — still net positive, not cancelled

how_to_run_full_scale_later.pattern: N processes with disjoint --seq-start/--seq-end, distinct --out-dir, same --limit/corpus/max-layer/max-seq-len, then merge_fullseq_capture_shards.py
how_to_run_full_scale_later.coordinate: Do not overlap with live v0-l1-capture-parallel or glm-floats-safe lanes; schedule after those finish or use disjoint GPU time.

not_recommended: Layer multi-worker sharding without residual handoff
Assuming 28-worker linear speedup (Metal + RAM will collapse efficiency)

glm_teacher_forced_investigation.architecture: Layer-major donor capture: stream one layer's weights, run that layer over ALL sequences (microbatch), seal carry, evict, advance. Double-buffer N-1/N/N+1 prefetch.
glm_teacher_forced_investigation.bottleneck_character: Different from DSV4F: weight-shard I/O + layer residency dominate (official MoE body is multi-hundred-GB streamed). Sequence multi-process would multiply weight streaming unless weights stay resident (--no-evict) and RAM allows. Intra-layer microbatch already amortizes a resident layer across sequences.
glm_teacher_forced_investigation.recommendation: Do not copy DSV4F process-sharding blindly onto GLM. Prefer larger --microbatch and keeping the layer-major stream single-process; if multi-worker is attempted, shard sequences only with --no-evict and shared warm stream root, measure I/O amplification first. No multi-worker GLM change shipped in this task.

code_changes.change: Added --seq-start/--seq-end/--worker-id/--min-layer; shard provenance in receipt; skip shared repo receipt path when sharding; refuse min_layer>0
New merge tool: traces + npy concat + merged receipt with worker provenance

Serial baseline: synthetic 4 seq max-layer 1 export (wall ~9.1s)

confidence.notes: Correctness is high confidence (byte-identical npy + matching site hashes). Speedup is real but measured under a competing full-stack L1 capture; idle-machine speedups likely higher for 2w and possibly 4w. Production N still needs a clean remeasure.
